title: Emergency Hyperkalemia Algorithm
subtitle: Stabilize membrane → shift K+ → remove K+

steps.title: Recognize severity
steps.body: Check ECG for peaked T waves, widened QRS, sine wave pattern, or muscle weakness. K+ ≥6.5 mEq/L or any ECG changes = emergency.
steps.tip: ECG changes mean treat before waiting for repeat labs.

steps.title: Stabilize the myocardium
steps.body: Give IV calcium gluconate 1–2 g (or calcium chloride in cardiac arrest). Onset in 1–3 minutes; does not lower potassium.
steps.tip: Calcium is temporizing — always follow with K+ lowering therapy.

steps.title: Shift potassium intracellularly
steps.body: Insulin 10 units + D50, and/or albuterol nebulizer, and/or sodium bicarbonate if acidotic. Expect transient drop of ~0.5–1.0 mEq/L.
steps.tip: Monitor glucose every 30–60 min after insulin.

steps.title: Remove potassium
steps.body: Loop diuretics if volume responsive, patiromer/sodium zirconium cyclosilicate if stable, kayexalate if needed, or hemodialysis for refractory or ESRD.
steps.tip: Dialysis is definitive in anuric AKI or ESRD.

steps.title: Treat the cause
steps.body: Stop ACEi/ARB, spironolactone, NSAIDs, trimethoprim; treat acidosis, tissue breakdown, or obstruction. Recheck K+ and ECG after each intervention.
steps.tip: Repeat ECG after calcium and after K+ shifts.
